newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon deal under closer scrutiny - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon deal under closer scrutiny - WSJ.

text.p: Pentagon officials may seek major changes to Raytheon Co's proposed acquisition of General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp defense unit because of concerns about the effect on the missile business, according to Friday's electronic edition of the Wall Street Journal.

According to unnamed people familiar with the situation, the Justice Department last week made a sweeping request for new information on the proposed $9.5 billion deal. The Journal said such a formal step often signals anti-trust concerns.

In particular, the Defense Department is most concerned with the concentration the deal would create in the missile business, particularly the electronic brains and sensors used in missiles, the sources told the Journal.
Under a 1994 agreement, defense-company mergers are reviewed by the Justice Department, the Federal Trade Commission and the Pentagon.
The Journal quoted an unnamed Pentagon official as saying that there is "a lot of angst here about folding all of the missile business into Raytheon."
If the acquisition is approved, Raytheon, which is based in Lexington, Mass., would dominate air-to-missile production.

The Pentagon official said there are three possible options: opposing the acquisition in its entirety; requiring part of the missile business to be set up as a separate company; or setting up barriers within Raytheon's missile operations to prevent the sharing of competitive information.
